emails.subject: URGENT: Temperature Excursion - DNL593 Study #2023-DNL-301 - Site 1047
emails.body:
Good morning,

I am reporting an urgent temperature excursion event that occurred overnight in our pharmacy investigational product refrigerator.

DETAILS:
- Study: DNL593-301
- Site Number: 1047
- Discovery Time: 07:00 today (March 14, 2024)
- Refrigerator: IP Fridge #2 (dedicated to DNL593 storage)
- Issue: Refrigerator malfunction - door seal failure detected

Our temperature monitoring system alarmed at approximately 02:15 this morning, but the pharmacy was not staffed until 07:00. Upon arrival, I found the refrigerator temperature reading 15°C (should be 2-8°C).

We have:
- Immediately transferred all DNL593 vials to backup refrigerator (validated, temp stable)
- Documented the event with photos and temperature logs
- Secured the malfunctioning unit

We currently have 18 vials of DNL593 that were stored in the affected refrigerator. I need urgent guidance on:
1. Whether these vials can still be dispensed to patients
2. What documentation you require from us
3. Whether we need to quarantine all affected product

We have two patients scheduled for dosing tomorrow (March 15) and need to know if we can proceed.

Please advise urgently.

Best regards,
Sarah Martinez, PharmD
Clinical Trials Pharmacist
Regional Clinical Trials Unit
Phone: +1-555-0147

emails.subject: RE: URGENT: Temperature Excursion - DNL593 Study #2023-DNL-301 - Site 1047
emails.body:
Dear Sarah,

Thank you for the prompt notification. I am looping in the sponsor QA team and we are treating this as a priority issue.

To properly assess the impact, please provide the following information as soon as possible:

1. TEMPERATURE DATA:
   - Complete temperature log from the monitoring system (last 24 hours minimum)
   - Exact time the temperature first exceeded 8°C
   - Maximum temperature reached
   - Duration of excursion

2. AFFECTED PRODUCT:
   - Complete list of vial numbers stored in the affected refrigerator
   - Lot numbers for all affected vials
   - Expiration dates
   - Current drug accountability records showing which vials are assigned to which patients

3. DOCUMENTATION:
   - Photos of the refrigerator temperature display
   - Photos of the alarm system showing alert time
   - Maintenance records for this refrigerator (last calibration/validation)

Please DO NOT dispense any product from the affected refrigerator until we provide clearance. Place all 18 vials on quarantine status immediately.

For your scheduled patients tomorrow, we will work to provide a decision by end of day today (5 PM EST). If needed, we can arrange emergency shipment of replacement product overnight.

I will schedule a conference call for 2 PM EST today with sponsor medical and quality teams. Dial-in details to follow.

Regards,
James Wong
Clinical Operations Manager
PharmaTrial CRO
Mobile: +1-555-0198

emails.subject: RE: URGENT: Temperature Excursion - DNL593 Study #2023-DNL-301 - Site 1047 - Stability Assessment
emails.body:
Team,

I have reviewed the temperature excursion data with our CMC and stability teams. Here is the preliminary assessment prior to our 2 PM call:

STABILITY DATA SUMMARY:
DNL593 (50mg/mL) has been tested under accelerated stability conditions:
- Storage at 25°C/60% RH: Stable for up to 7 days (no degradation >2%)
- Storage at 40°C/75% RH: Stable for up to 48 hours

EXCURSION ASSESSMENT:
- Maximum temperature: 16.2°C
- Duration at >8°C: ~5 hours
- This falls well within our stability envelope

PRELIMINARY CONCLUSION:
From a product stability and patient safety perspective, the affected vials remain suitable for use. The excursion was:
1. Relatively brief (5 hours)
2. Moderate temperature (max 16.2°C, well below accelerated stability test conditions)
3. Single event (not repeated exposure)
4. Well-documented

HOWEVER, we must still address:
1. Regulatory reporting requirements (protocol deviation)
2. Quality system documentation
3. Root cause analysis and CAPA
4. Whether this constitutes a reportable event to IRB/EC

I recommend we proceed with the affected product for patient dosing, but we need QA sign-off and proper documentation in place.

See you all on the call in 45 minutes.

Dr. Rajesh Patel, MD, PhD
Medical Monitor
MedSponsor Pharmaceuticals
Direct: +1-555-0234

emails.subject: RE: URGENT: Temperature Excursion - DNL593 Study #2023-DNL-301 - Site 1047 - QA Assessment
emails.body:
All,

Thank you for the productive call. This email serves as official documentation of our decisions and action items.

DECISION: PRODUCT APPROVED FOR USE

Based on the stability data presented by Dr. Patel and the thorough documentation provided by Site 1047, Quality Assurance approves the continued use of the 18 affected DNL593 vials (Lot DNL593-2023-B047, vials 001-1047-0023 through 001-1047-0040).

RATIONALE:
1. Temperature excursion (max 16.2°C for 5 hours) is within validated stability parameters
2. Product integrity is not compromised
3. No patient safety concerns identified
4. Complete documentation and traceability maintained

REQUIRED ACTIONS:

Site 1047 (Sarah Martinez):
□ Complete Temperature Excursion Report Form (TERF-001) - Due: March 15, 2024
□ Submit Protocol Deviation Report (minor deviation) - Due: March 18, 2024
□ Update drug accountability log to note excursion event for affected vials
□ Add notation in dispensing records when these vials are used
□ Complete root cause analysis with maintenance contractor - Due: March 21, 2024
□ Implement CAPA: Enhanced monitoring procedures and backup alarm notification - Due: March 28, 2024
□ Provide maintenance/repair report for affected refrigerator - Due: March 18, 2024

CRO (James Wong):
□ Submit protocol deviation to sponsor within 5 business days
□ Ensure site completes all required documentation
□ Track CAPA implementation
□ Update site monitoring report

Sponsor (MedSponsor):
□ Review and approve protocol deviation report
□ Determine if IRB notification required (Regulatory to assess) - Due: March 15, 2024
□ File temperature excursion in TMF
□ Update risk management plan if needed

REGULATORY REPORTING:
Our regulatory team will assess whether this event requires IRB notification. Preliminary assessment: likely NOT reportable as it does not impact patient safety and product remains within specifications. Final determination by COB tomorrow.

SITE MAY PROCEED WITH SCHEDULED PATIENT VISITS ON MARCH 15.

The affected vials are released from quarantine status and may be dispensed per protocol.

Please confirm receipt of this email and acknowledge action items.

Best regards,

Michelle Torres
Senior Quality Assurance Manager
MedSponsor Pharmaceuticals
Email: michelle.torres@medsponsor.com
Phone: +1-555-0267
